protocol.incremental: 3x single-file touch on indexed db (3 distinct files)
protocol.isolation: each run in a fresh python subprocess; PYTHONPATH=src
protocol.rss: GetProcessMemoryInfo PeakWorkingSetSize inside the measuring process

findings: Zero parse failures and zero syntax-error files across all 2274 Java files indexed (clean upstream corpora).
jgit cold ~13.2 files/s; peak RSS ~1 GB at 1.9k files (parser-cache JSON + graph build dominate).
warm is SLOWER than cold at jgit scale (31.7s vs 24.9s) - replace_snapshot delete+insert on a large existing db costs more than building fresh.

incremental offers NO benefit at gson/jgit scale (2.9s vs 2.8s; 33.3s vs 24.9s): a single-file touch invalidates a large affected-reference set (short-name collisions across packages), forcing near-full re-resolution. This is a real cost characteristic of the current incremental design on Java corpora and is a key input to the P4 ADR.
No pre-existing PASS threshold was violated or invented: the plan set no absolute budget; raw numbers are reported as measurements.
